hardware_note: Benchmark runs entirely offline with no network. The learning subsystem is deterministic and lightweight; these numbers are from this sandbox. On the Windows target (i7 6th gen, 8GB RAM) the CPU-only numbers will be similar because the subsystem does no LLM inference — all grading is rule-based and all reference solutions are computed by the existing deterministic engines.

metrics.interpretation: The evidence-based engine reaches the exact expected level (novice/apprentice/practitioner) for 5 known evidence sequences, including the rule that viewing does not raise mastery.
Re-solving the SAME exercise 5 times leaves the distinct-exercise count at 1; mastery does not inflate to practitioner (which needs 2+ distinct exercises).

Correct answer with reasoning -> correct; bare number -> not correct; wrong law with right-looking number -> not correct; unsupported assumption -> not correct. The central 'do not reward correct answer for incorrect reasoning' rule holds.
Every generated engine exercise (ohm, series/parallel, voltage divider, RC) has a reference solution that matches an independent engine computation to within rounding.
The hint-level explanation never contains the reference solution value across 5 exercises.
Evidence (an independent solve + a view) survives reopening a learning session with the same profile name; the DB is the source of truth.
The SM-2 scheduler is a pure function: 20 runs with identical inputs produced exactly 1 distinct output.
An unconfirmed repair case stays unconfirmed; the root cause is not disclosed; the generated follow-up exercise hides its solution.
Every generated exercise carries a source_kind (engine/kb/confirmed_case/synthetic) and a source_ref.
The subsystem imports and runs with no network; the existing repair flow ('learn record', 'orchestrate', 'analyze') is unchanged.

what_this_proves: Mastery is evidence-based: viewing an explanation 10 times does NOT raise mastery; only independent solves and new-context demonstrations do.
A correct final answer reached by incorrect reasoning is NOT counted as correct (the spec's central rule).
Exercises always carry a known reference solution computed by a deterministic engine; the LLM is never the source of a numerical reference value.
The hint level never discloses the solution; the default level is 'guided' (not full).
Spaced review is deterministic and performance-based (SM-2): failures reset the interval, successes grow it by the ease factor.
Repair-to-learning conversion never marks an uncertain outcome as confirmed and never auto-discloses the original solution.
The subsystem is fully offline and additive — the existing repair/diagnostic flow is unchanged.
limitations: The reasoning evaluator is rule-based and heuristic: it checks for the presence of the relevant law/keyword and a reasoning connective. A subtly-wrong reasoning phrased with the right keywords could slip through. This is a deliberate trade-off for offline determinism.

Mastery thresholds (apprentice=2 indep, practitioner=3 indep + 2 distinct, expert=5 indep + 4 distinct + 2 new-context) are calibrated for a learning context, not a formal certification. They are conservative on purpose.

The exercise generator covers 16 skill categories but draws from 4 source generators (engine, KB, confirmed case, synthetic RC). Skills without a dedicated generator fall back to an open-ended prompt graded on reasoning.

The Socratic engine has built-in paths for 5 skills (ohm_kirchhoff, voltage_divider, mosfet, measurement_interp, fault_isolation); other skills use the exercise + hint/explain flow instead of a Socratic path.
